title: Purchasing groups
requirement: Purchasing groups shall be a master of the eProcurement Suite, not a unit kind: a group of buyers (people of BF-021), the categories it covers (BF-042) and the units it serves; a group serves several units and owns no records. A legal entity may name one purchasing group as its buying group, which serves the lines of its units that no other group's categories cover. The suite's products use a group to assign the buyer of a request line by the line's category and unit, to filter a buyer's work queue, and to report spend by group; a purchasing group gives no access and takes no part in approvals.
rationale: Buyers are organised by what they buy and for whom, across units. A unit kind would put a group at one place in the tree and make it an owner of records, and a purchasing group is neither. Only the eProcurement Suite assigns buyers, so the master is the suite's (ADR-0043).
acceptance_criteria: Given a purchasing group covering the category IT hardware and serving units A and B, When it is opened, Then its buyers, categories and units are listed.|Given a line of the category IT hardware in unit A, When a product asks which purchasing group serves it, Then the group and its buyers are named.|Given a legal entity whose buying group is G, and a line of one of its units whose category no group covers, When a product asks which purchasing group serves it, Then G and its buyers are named.|Given a buyer of a purchasing group, When they open a request of a unit their roles do not reach, Then it is refused, because the group grants no access. (error case)|Given a purchasing group, When someone tries to make it the owning organisation of a record, Then it is refused, because a purchasing group is no unit. (error case)
notes: Was BF-007, FF-002 and BF-061: BF-007 whole, with the buying group of BF-061's chart of accounts merged in as a legal entity's buying group. Moved at the review of L2, 2026-10-20 (ADR-0043). BF-007 was decided 2026-10-20: a purchasing group assigns the buyer, filters the work queue and reports spend; it is not access and not approvals.

title: Supplier purchasing profile
requirement: Every supplier of the Business supplier master (BF-101) shall have one purchasing profile, a one-to-one extension the eProcurement Suite owns: its match levels for products and for services (none, two-way or three-way), the channels its documents may reach it by (email, the supplier portal, internal only), its preferred or approved status per category (PUR-022) and its terms per organisation (PUR-023). The profile is made the first time the suite reads or writes the supplier, with the defaults the tenant set (PUR-024 for the match levels), and it has no life apart from its supplier.
rationale: The supplier record is the Foundation's, because any suite that pays a vendor needs it; how documents are matched and reach the supplier is buying's (ADR-0043). One profile per supplier keeps the two apart without a second list of suppliers.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier the suite has never read, When a buyer opens it, Then its purchasing profile exists with the tenant's defaults and is shown beside the supplier record.|Given a supplier with the match level two-way for services and the channel email, When an order is issued to it, Then the order's service lines are matched two-way and it goes by email.|Given a match level that is not none, two-way or three-way, or a channel the tenant has not enabled, When saved, Then it is refused naming the field. (error case)|Given a second purchasing profile for the same supplier, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-022 and BF-101, the match levels of its commercial defaults and its portal settings (the allowed channels), and its preferred flag, which is now per category (PUR-022). Moved at the review of L2, 2026-10-20 (ADR-0043).

title: Preferred status per category and supplier suggestions
requirement: A supplier's purchasing profile shall hold its preferred or approved status for each category it serves (BF-107), and the suite's supplier suggestions on request and order lines shall use them: the preferred suppliers of the line's category first, then the approved ones, never a supplier on hold. Where the tenant requires qualification for a category, a supplier may be preferred or approved for it only while it is qualified for it: this master asks through an extension point it declares, the qualification of a supplier for a scope, which answers qualified, not qualified, or not required; and when the product that qualifies suppliers reports that a qualification ended (disqualified, or its requalification lapsed), the status for that category is withdrawn and the buyer owner is told.
rationale: Guide buyers to the right suppliers. A preferred supplier that is not qualified for what it supplies sends buyers to the wrong place with the system's blessing; preferred status follows qualification in the leading suites and in ISO 9001's control of external providers (clause 8.4).
acceptance_criteria: Given a line of category X, When suppliers are suggested, Then the preferred suppliers for X appear first.|Given a supplier that no longer serves category X (BF-107), When suppliers are suggested for X, Then it does not appear, and its status for X is gone.|Given a supplier on hold, When suppliers are suggested, Then it is excluded.|Given a preferred status for a category the supplier does not serve, When saved, Then it is refused naming the category. (error case)|Given category X requires qualification and a supplier whose qualification for X is pending, When a buyer sets it preferred for X, Then it is refused naming the qualification. (error case)|Given a supplier preferred for X, When the qualifying product reports that its qualification for X ended, Then its status for X is withdrawn and the buyer owner is told.|Given no product that answers the qualification extension point, When a status is set, Then the answer is not required and today's rule applies.
notes: Was FF-038 and BF-107, the preferred status and the suggestions; the categories a supplier serves stay BF-107's. Moved at the review of L2, 2026-10-20 (ADR-0043). Changed 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G2 of the supplier management pack): preferred status only for qualified scopes. This master sits below the suite's products and never depends on one (ADR-0043), so it declares the extension point (section 8.5) and Supplier management implements it (SUP-181), and reports an ended qualification through this master's Contracts. Decision: a category the tenant has not marked as requiring qualification keeps today's rule, and so does a tenant without Supplier management; the owner confirms.

title: Purchasing terms per organisation
requirement: For each organisation in which a supplier is enabled (BF-108), its purchasing profile shall hold that organisation's match levels and preferred flag, which come before the supplier's own for documents of the organisation; the enablement and its other terms stay the Business PRD's.
rationale: One registration for the supplier, separate control for each unit.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier two-way for products with organisation A's terms three-way, When an order of A is approved, Then its product lines take three-way.|Given a supplier preferred in organisation A only, When suppliers are suggested for a line of organisation B, Then it is not shown as preferred.|Given a supplier not enabled in organisation B, When B's purchasing terms are saved for it, Then it is refused naming the missing enablement. (error case)
notes: Was FF-182 and BF-108, the match levels and the preferred flag of an organisation's terms. Moved at the review of L2, 2026-10-20 (ADR-0043).

title: Defaults of a new supplier's purchasing profile
requirement: Procurement administrators shall set the match levels a new supplier's purchasing profile starts with, applied when the profile is made and editable per supplier. The other defaults of a new supplier stay with their owners: payment terms and currency with the supplier master (BF-106), the sections and documents it must complete with Supplier management, its channels with the supplier portal.
acceptance_criteria: Given defaults set, When a supplier's profile is made, Then its match levels are pre-filled.|Given a default changed, When existing suppliers are viewed, Then their values are unchanged.|Given a user without the purchasing configuration permission, When saving the defaults, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-035 and BF-106, the match levels of a new supplier. Moved at the review of L2, 2026-10-20 (ADR-0043).

title: A legal entity's match levels, and the order they apply in
requirement: Procurement administrators shall set each legal entity's default match levels for products and for services. A document line takes its match level from the supplier's terms in the line's organisation (PUR-023), else from the supplier's purchasing profile (PUR-021), else from its legal entity's default; the products that stamp lines read them in this order.
rationale: Predictable matching, from one order of precedence.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier two-way and its legal entity three-way for products, When a product line's match level is resolved, Then it is two-way.|Given a supplier without a match level and its legal entity three-way for products, When a product line's match level is resolved, Then it is three-way.|Given a match level that is not none, two-way or three-way, When saved for a legal entity, Then it is refused naming the field. (error case)
notes: Was FF-002 and BF-061, the default match levels for products and services of a legal entity's chart of accounts, which the purchasing master now holds for the legal entity. Moved at the review of L2, 2026-10-20, with the other match levels (ADR-0043).

title: Supplier segments
requirement: A supplier's purchasing profile shall hold one segment: strategic, preferred, approved or transactional. The tenant's segment rules set it each night from the supplier's spend over the last twelve months (by bands), its categories and its risk tier, the first matching rule winning; a permitted user may set it by hand with a reason, and a segment set by hand stays until it is changed by hand, with the rules' proposal shown beside it. A new supplier starts as transactional. Lists, reviews and reports filter by segment, and the segment report shows the strategic share: strategic suppliers as a share of active suppliers. The facts only a product holds, a supplier's risk tier and its spend, come through an extension point this master declares, the supplier facts for segment rules, which Supplier management implements.
rationale: Not every supplier deserves the same attention: a segment tells buyers and reviewers where to spend their time, and the strategic share is a benchmark of its own (APQC measure 103199, median 20 percent). The segment is buying's, not the Foundation's (ADR-0043, decision 8).
acceptance_criteria: Given a rule that a supplier with more than 1,000,000 of spend in twelve months is strategic, and a supplier with 1,200,000, When the rules run, Then its segment is strategic, with the rule named as its reason.|Given a segment set by hand with a reason, When the rules run and propose another, Then the segment stays and the rules' proposal is shown beside it.|Given 40 strategic suppliers among 200 active ones, When the segment report runs, Then the strategic share is 20 percent.|Given a segment set by hand without a reason, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a rule on the risk tier and no product that answers the supplier facts, When the rules run, Then that rule is skipped and reported as unavailable, and no segment changes because of it. (error case)
notes: New 2026-10-21 (SUP-gaps, gap G9 of the supplier management pack). The risk tier is Supplier management's (SUP-007), and so is the twelve-month spend it keeps from the order events it already hears (SUP-062); this master asks for both through the extension point of section 8.5 and never depends on a product (ADR-0043). Decision: rules run nightly, the first matching rule wins, a segment set by hand wins over the rules until changed by hand, and a new supplier starts as transactional; the owner confirms.

title: A person's purchasing profile
requirement: Each person of the people master (BF-021) may have a purchasing profile holding their default ship-to location (BF-081), offered first on the documents they raise in the eProcurement Suite; the person's default account string stays on the person (BF-021).
rationale: Requesters have things delivered to the same place again and again. The ship-to is buying's; the person is the Foundation's (ADR-0043).
acceptance_criteria: Given a person whose default ship-to is L, When they start a request, Then L is offered first.|Given an inactive ship-to location, When it is saved as a person's default, Then it is refused naming the location. (error case)|Given a person's default ship-to deactivated later, When they start a request, Then no default is offered and the line asks for one.
notes: Was BF-021, the default ship-to location. Moved at the review of L2, 2026-10-20 (ADR-0043).

title: The eProcurement Suite's approval starter set
requirement: The eProcurement Suite shall bring a starter set of approval configurations for the document types its products register (manager chain by amount bands, budget owner for requests, finance for invoices above a threshold, procurement head for suppliers), on the approval configurations of BF-141, seeded as inactive examples that administrators can activate and edit; a tenant without the suite (TF-244) has none of them.
rationale: Faster go-live. A starter set is a suite's content, and the configuration that holds it is the Foundation's mechanism (ADR-0043).
acceptance_criteria: Given a new tenant with the suite, When the console opens, Then the starter configurations exist inactive.|Given activation, When a document is submitted, Then the configuration applies.|Given an edit, When saved, Then it is versioned by the kernel workflow.|Given a starter configuration edited to reference an unknown field, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a tenant without the suite, When the console opens, Then none of the suite's starter configurations exist.
notes: Was FF-174 and BF-201. Moved at the review of L2, 2026-10-20 (ADR-0043): a starter set is a suite's content; BF-141 keeps the mechanism.

title: The eProcurement Suite's readiness items
requirement: The eProcurement Suite shall contribute its items to the tenant readiness view (BF-202) and to a new organisation's checklist (BF-203): approved suppliers enabled in the organisations that buy, items or catalogues, purchasing groups covering the categories in use, match levels set for the legal entities or their suppliers, and the suite's starter approval configurations activated or replaced, each with a link to where it is fixed.
rationale: Goal 3 of the Business PRD (a first request within one day) is the suite's goal; its checklist items are its content (ADR-0043).
acceptance_criteria: Given no purchasing group, When the readiness view loads, Then the item is listed with a link to the purchasing groups.|Given every item of the suite complete, When the view loads, Then the suite's part shows ready.|Given a tenant without the suite (TF-244), When the view loads, Then none of the suite's items are listed.|Given the suite's module switched off for the tenant, When the view loads, Then its items show as unavailable, never as ready. (error case)
notes: Was FF-175, BF-202, FF-188 and BF-203: the suppliers and items of BF-202's checklist and the enabled suppliers of BF-203's, now the suite's contribution with its own items. Moved at the review of L2, 2026-10-20 (ADR-0043).
